title: Provenance receipts
text: RFC 8785, JSON Canonicalization Scheme: object keys sorted UTF-16 code units; strings escaped JSON requires (", \, \b \t \n \f \r, control characters \u00xx lowercase hex); numbers ECMAScript’s shortest round-trip form, plain decimal 1e-7 1e21 exponent form outside (1e+21, 1e-7, 333333333.3333333); whitespace. Two things trip implementations. Read every JSON number double: Python’s json reads 1152921504606846976 int, rfc8785 refuses past 2^53, parse parse_int=float. shortest spelling needs correctly rounded decimal parser: R’s .numeric() misread 84% 200,000 random 17-digit spellings arm64 macOS, long double double, crate reads candidates back jsonlite, uses C library’s strtod.

text: crt_receipt_compare() reads receipt register, one row per field, decide difference : refuse makes verdict different, warn reported without changing , record listed . Every recipe field refuses, recipe_id covers ; every context field recorded. comparison receipts alone certifies less one re-reads result. title: Canonical Schemas and Data Governance for Changing Data
text: call crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", path), five pieces wire together runtime: Registry (inst/extdata/crate_registry.csv) — CSV mapping (source, file_name) pair handler function name schema YAML path. crate looks “know file?” . Loaded crt_registry_load(). Schema YAML (inst/extdata/schemas/bcfp/user_habitat_classification.yaml) — declares canonical column shape (names, types, required flags) known upstream variant (column-name set + normalize-function id). Loaded crt_schema_read(). Handler (R/crt_handler_bcfp_user_habitat_classification.R) — one function per (source, file_name). crate matches actual file columns variant’s declared columns (first set-equal match wins), dispatches matched variant_id handler: 2026-04-26-wide → identity passthrough (already canonical) pre-2026-04-26-long → pivot long rows wide canonical, mapping habitat_ind text values integer indicators Validation (crt_schema_validate()) — handler returns, crate checks every column declared required: true schema present. Fails loud listing missing required columns. Type enforcement (crt_schema_apply()) — finally, crate coerces every named column type declared schema (integer, double, string, logical, datetime). Schema YAML single source truth types; handlers don’t encode type knowledge. Without , readr’s defaults leak (integer cols become double, declared strings become Date). Steps 4 5 crt_schema_conform(), crt_ingest() calls rather reimplements — file frame supply get identical treatment. datetime column instant, crate never moves . POSIXct timezone attribute stamped UTC rather converted: several readers return correct UTC instants carrying timezone label, R renders session’s zone read second clock second timezone. Converting “fix” rendering injects real whole-hour error every join downstream. Stamping fixes label, thing wrong. handler made type change transparent example. wide canonical declares spawning rearing integer columns; long upstream habitat_ind text ("t"/"f"). pivot text→integer conversion step long→wide reshape — callers never see either intermediate form. Type enforcement (step 5) catches leaks boundary regardless handler.

code: # Read the bundled wide-format fixture (today's upstream shape) wide_path <- system.file(   "extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_wide.csv",   package = "crate" ) wide <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", wide_path) wide #> # A tibble: 6 × 11 #>   blue_line_key downstream_route_measure upstream_route_measure #>           <int>                    <dbl>                  <dbl> #> 1     356385867                        0                    208 #> 2     356385867                        0                    208 #> 3     356400111                      500                   1500 #> 4     356400111                      500                   1500 #> 5     356500222                        0                    800 #> 6     356600333                        0                    300 #> # ℹ 8 more variables: watershed_group_code <chr>, species_code <chr>, #> #   spawning <int>, rearing <int>, reviewer_name <chr>, review_date <chr>, #> #   source <chr>, notes <chr>  # Read the bundled long-format fixture (historical pre-2026-04-26 shape). # crt_ingest pivots it to canonical wide automatically - same call, # same output shape, regardless of which upstream variant arrived. long_path <- system.file(   "extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_long.csv",   package = "crate" ) long <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification", long_path) long #> # A tibble: 5 × 11 #>   blue_line_key downstream_route_measure upstream_route_measure #>           <int>                    <dbl>                  <dbl> #> 1     356385867                        0                    208 #> 2     356385867                        0                    208 #> 3     356400111                      500                   1500 #> 4     356400111                      500                   1500 #> 5     356500222                        0                    800 #> # ℹ 8 more variables: watershed_group_code <chr>, species_code <chr>, #> #   spawning <int>, rearing <int>, reviewer_name <chr>, review_date <chr>, #> #   source <chr>, notes <chr>  # Both calls return the same canonical column set identical(names(wide), names(long)) #> [1] TRUE  # NGE fish data: a 2023 file, with PIT tags written into its comments, and # a 2024 field sheet read to the same columns, so the seasons stack and a # tagged fish can be followed between them. fish_2023 <- crt_ingest("nge", "fish_data", system.file(   "extdata/examples/nge/fish_data_2023_peace.csv", package = "crate" )) fish_2024 <- crt_ingest("nge", "fish_data", system.file(   "extdata/examples/nge/fish_data_2024.csv", package = "crate" )) fish <- rbind(fish_2023, fish_2024) fish[!is.na(fish$pit_tag_id), c("local_name", "species", "length_mm", "pit_tag_id")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   local_name    species       length_mm pit_tag_id     #>   <chr>         <chr>             <dbl> <chr>          #> 1 100001_us_ef1 Rainbow Trout       157 3DD.003E190001 #> 2 100002_ds_ef1 Dolly Varden         92 3DD.003E190002 #> 3 100001_us_ef1 Rainbow Trout       201 3DD.003E190001
